source: Marcura Maritime Scope 3 Strategy Report, Section 6 (Feature Comparison) and Section 5 (Competitive Positioning)
positioning_summary: Plotting competitors on two axes — general-purpose versus maritime-specialised, and developer infrastructure versus enterprise platform — makes the opportunity visible in a way a feature list cannot. Marcura's desired position sits closer to Searoutes and Sinay in maritime specificity, but is pulled toward the platform end of the vertical axis by owning supplier engagement and procurement workflows that neither currently offers. No competitor reviewed occupies this position today.
feature_comparison_summary: No competitor is strong on both supplier engagement and procurement workflows simultaneously — the exact pairing identified as the highest-value, lowest-competition opportunity in this assessment. That gap, not calculation capability, is where Marcura's differentiation should concentrate.
customer_value_proposition: Feature comparisons describe capability; they do not explain why a buyer chooses one vendor over another. Each competitor's adoption is driven by relief from a specific compliance or operational burden, not by carbon calculation as a category. Marcura's proposition should be framed the same way: not 'a maritime Scope 3 platform,' but compliance-ready emissions data delivered inside the systems ship operators and their suppliers already use.
differentiation_points: Maritime specialisation not offered by general-purpose Scope 3 platforms
Procurement-to-emissions integration (purchase order line to emission event to Scope 3 allocation)
Supplier-level Scope 3 visibility combined with supplier engagement workflows
Audit-ready calculation traceability (activity value, factor source/version, calculation formula on every record)
Decision support (recommendations, reduction opportunities) rather than measurement alone
